The magnitude of the charge on each half is& $\left|Q\right| = {10}^{3}{ε}_{0}$, where ${ε}_{0}$~is the permittivity of free the space. The net electric field at the centre& $O$& is

$⇒$ due to a charge arc, electric field at centre is given by

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $r$ is the orbital radius and $v$& is the orbital velocity of an electron in a hydrogen atom, then its magnetic dipole moment is
questions.solution:
The magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron: The electron of change (−e) performs uniforms circular motion around a stationary& heavy nucleus of charge +Ze. This constitutes a current I.

$∴$ $I = \dfrac{e}{T}$...(i)

Where, T is the time period of revolution. Let r be the orbital radius of electron and v the orbital speed. Then

$T = \dfrac{2\pir}{υ}$...(ii)

Substituting the value of T in (i), we get

$I = \dfrac{e}{\dfrac{2\pir}{υ}} = \dfrac{eυ}{2\pir}$

The magnetic moment (m) associated with this circular current is

$m = I\pir^{2}[ ∵ \overset{→}{m} = I\overset{→}{A} ]$

$∴$ $m = \dfrac{eυ}{2\pir} ⋅ \pir^{2} = \dfrac{eυr}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin spherical shell of radius $R$ is cut into two equal halves and then each of its halves is charged to the same uniform surface charge density $\sigma$. If $F$ is the force exerted on each half to keep them at equilibrium, then $F$& is& proportional to
questions.solution:
Electrical force per unit area = $\dfrac{1}{2} {ε}_{0} E^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} {ε}_{0} {\left(\dfrac{σ}{{ε}_{0}}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{σ}^{2}}{2 {ε}_{0}}$

Projected area = $π R^{2}$

$∴$ Net electrical force = $\left(\dfrac{{σ}^{2}}{2 {ε}_{0}}\right) \left(π R^{2}\right)$

In equilibrium, this force should be equal to the applied force.

$∴\text{F} = \dfrac{π {σ}^{2} R^{2}}{2 {ε}_{0}}$

or $\text{F} ∝ \dfrac{{σ}^{2} R^{2}}{{ε}_{0}}$

questions.q: In a uniform magnetic field of strength $0. 15T$, a short bar magnet of magnetic moment $m = 0. 32{J T}^{- 1}$ is placed. The potential energy of the magnet in its unstable equilibrium position is
questions.solution:
For the unstable equilibrium, the angle between the magnetic moment and magnetic field is 180^{o}. ( $∵$ In this position it will be in a direction perpendicular to magnetic field thus maximum torque will act on it.)

$\theta = 1 8 {0}^{o}$

Potential energy of the magnet

U = - mB cos 180^{o}

= - 0.32 x 0.15 (- 1) = 4.8 x 10^{-2} J

Thus, for the unstable equilibrium the potential energy is 4.8 x 10^{-2} J.

questions.q: If the magnetic moment and the pole strength of a bar magnet are $3.6 \times {10}^{- 3}Am^{2}$ and $120 \times {10}^{- 3}Am$, then its magnetic length is
questions.solution:
For a bar magnet, the magnetic moment is

$M = polestrength \times magneticlength$

So the magnetic length will be

${l}_{mag} = \dfrac{M}{m}$

$⇒ {l}_{mag} = \dfrac{3.6 \times {10}^{- 3}}{120 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 3 \times {10}^{- 2}m = 3cm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnetic needle free to rotate in a horizontal plane is placed at the centre of a circular current-carrying coil whose axis is perpendicular to the magnetic meridian at that place. It is also known that the magnetic declination at this place is zero and in this condition, the magnetic needle is pointing towards the north-west. Now, if we reverse the direction of current in the coil, then the magnetic needle will
questions.solution: If there is no current in the coil, then the needle would point north but due to the magnetic field of the coil, it is pointing north-west. This means the magnetic field due to the coil is towards west and it is equal to the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field. So when we reverse the direction of current the magnetic field due to the coil will be towards east and the magnetic needle will point north-east.

When the same material is placed in an external magnetic field of intensity $\text{0}\text{.2 T}$ at a temperature of $\text{16 K}$, the& magnetization will be

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance of two points on the axis of a magnet from its centre is $10$ cm and $20$ cm respectively. The ratio of magnetic intensity at these points is $12. 5: 1$. The length of the magnet will be
questions.solution:
The magnetic field on the axis of a bar magnet of length $2l$, having a pole strength $m$, at a distance $d$ is

$B = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m}{\left[d - l\right]2} - \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m}{\left[d + l\right]2}$

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}m}{4\pi}\dfrac{\left[d + l\right]2 - \left[d - l\right]2}{\left[d^{2} - l^{2}\right]2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}mld}{\pi\left[d^{2} - l^{2}\right]2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B1}{B2} = \dfrac{d1}{d2}\left[\dfrac{{d}_{2}^{2} - l^{2}}{{d}_{1}^{2} - l^{2}}\right]2$

$⇒ \dfrac{12.5}{1} = \dfrac{10}{20}\left[\dfrac{400 - l^{2}}{100 - l^{2}}\right]2$

$⇒ l = 5 cm$

Hence, length of magnet $= 2l = 10 cm$

The least value of magnetic field strength required to magnetize is nickel because it is a ferromagnetic material. $Ni$ is a ferromagnetic substance which gets strongly magnetized when placed in an external magnetic field. When external magnetic field ${B}_{0}$, is applied the magnetic domains orient themselves in the direction of magnetic filed and grow in size.

Hence, $Ni$ requires least value of magnetic strength. $NaCl$ is a diamagnetic material. Its field lines are repelled.

questions.q: Two bar magnets $A$ and $B$ are placed one over the other and are allowed to Vibrate in a vibration magnetometer. They make $20$ oscillations per minute when the similar poles of $A$ and $B$ are on the same side, while they make $15$ oscillations per minute when their opposite poles lie on the same side. If ${M}_{A}$ and ${M}_{B}_{}are the magnetic moments of $ A$ and $B$ and if ${M}_{A}> {M}_{B}$, the ratio of ${M}_{A}$ and ${M}_{B}$ \text{ and } is$
questions.solution:
Ratio of magnetic moments of two magnets of equal size when in same and different position is
&
$\dfrac{{M}_{A}}{{M}_{B}} = \dfrac{{T}_d^{2} + {T}_s^{2}}{{T}_d^{2} - {T}_s^{2}} = \dfrac{{v ⁡}_d^{2} + {v ⁡}_s^{2}}{{v ⁡}_d^{2} - {v ⁡}_s^{2}}$

$\dfrac{{M}_{A}}{{M}_{B}} = \dfrac{2 {0}^{2} + 1 {5}^{2}}{2 {0}^{2} - 1 {5}^{2}}$

& & & & & & $= \dfrac{400 + 225}{400 - 225}$

${M}_{A}: {M}_{B} = 25: 7$

questions.q: A vibration magnetometer consists of two identical bar magnets placed one over the other such that they are mutually perpendicular and bisect each other. The time period of the combination is $4s$. If one of the magnets is removed, then the time period of other one will be
questions.solution:
As magnets are perpendicular to each other, the resultant magnetic moment

$M ' = \sqrt{M^{2} + M^{2}} = \sqrt{2}M$

$∴ {T}_{1} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{2I}{\left(\sqrt{2}M\right)H}}$

In the second case, ${T}_{2} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MH}}$

$\dfrac{T2}{T1} = \dfrac{1}{\left(2\right)1 / 4}$

$∴ {T}_{2} = \dfrac{4}{\left(2\right)1 / 4} = \text{3.36}s$

questions.q: Two short bar magnets of dipole moments $M$ and $M\sqrt{3}$ are joined at right angles to form a cross as depicted in the figure. The value of $\theta$ for which the system remains in equilibrium in a uniform external magnetic field $B$,& is

$tan ⁡ \theta = \sqrt{3} = tan ⁡ 60 °$

$∴ \theta = 60 °$

questions.q: A magnet is cut in four equal parts by cutting it parallel to its length. The time period of each part, if the time period of the original magnet in the same field is ${T}_{0}$, will be

$∴ \dfrac{T1}{T} = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A deflection magnetometer is placed with its arm along the east-west direction and a bar magnet is placed along the arm of the magnetometer. Due to the magnet, the deflection observed is $\theta$ and the period of oscillation of the needle in the magnetometer is $T$. When the magnet is removed, the period of oscillation is ${T}_{0}$. The relation between $T$ and ${T}_{0}$ is
questions.solution:
In the usual setting of deflection magnetometer, field due to magnet ($F$) and horizontal component ($H$) of earth's field are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the net field on the magnetic needle is $\sqrt{F^{2} + H^{2}}$

$∴ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M\sqrt{F^{2} + H^{2}}}}$ ...(i)

When the magnet is removed,

${T}_{0} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MH}}$ ...(ii)

Also, $\dfrac{F}{H} = tan ⁡ \theta$

Dividing (i) by (ii), we get

$\dfrac{T}{T0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{H}{F^{2} + H^{2}}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{H}{H^{2}\tan^{2} ⁡ \theta + H^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{H}{H\sqrt{\sec^{2} ⁡ \theta}}} = \sqrt{cos ⁡ \theta}$

$\begin{cases}⇒ T^{2}{T}_{0}^{2} = cos ⁡ \theta & ∴ T^{2} = {T}_{0}^{2}cos ⁡ \theta\end{cases}$

questions.q: A magnetic compass needle oscillates $30$ times per minute at a place where the dip is $45 °$ and $40$ times per minute where the dip is $30 °$. If ${B}_{1}$ and ${B}_{2}$ are the net magnetic fields due to the earth at the two places respectively, then the ratio ${B}_{1} / {B}_{2}$ is approximately equal to
questions.solution:
Let ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}$ be the respective oscillation frequencies respectively for $45 °$ and $30 °$ dip. Then,

${f}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{M{B}_{1}cos45 °}{I}}$

${f}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{M{B}_{2}cos30 °}{I}}$

$\dfrac{f1}{f2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{B}_{1}cos45 °}{{B}_{2}cos30 °}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{302}{402} = \dfrac{{B}_{1}cos45 °}{{B}_{2}cos30 °}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B1}{B2} = \dfrac{900 \times cos30 °}{1600 \times cos45 °}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B1}{B2} = 0.688 \approx 0.7$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnetic needle of negligible breadth and thickness compared to its length, oscillates in a horizontal plane with a period $T$. The period of oscillation of each part obtained on breaking the magnet into $n$& equal parts and perpendicular to the length is
questions.solution:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}}$

on breaking n equal parts perpendicular to length

$I′ = \dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right){\left(\dfrac{l}{n}\right)}^{2}$ of each part

$I′ = \dfrac{I}{n^{3}}, M′ = \dfrac{M}{n}$

$\dfrac{T^{′}}{T} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I^{′}}{M^{′}} \times \dfrac{M}{I}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{n^{3}} \times n} = \dfrac{1}{n} ⇒ T^{′} = \dfrac{T}{n}$

questions.q: A bar magnet has a magnetic moment equal to $5 \times {10}^{- 5}Wbm$. It is suspended in a magnetic field which has a magnetic induction $B = 8\pi \times {10}^{- 4}\text{T}$. The magnet vibrates with a period of vibration equal to $\text{15 s}$. The moment of inertia of magnet is
questions.solution:
Here, magnetic moment is given in weber-meter, which is the unit of ${\mu}_{0}M$.

$∴ {\mu}_{0}M = 5 \times {10}^{- 5}$ Wb-m

$M = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 5}}{{\mu}_{0}}Am^{2}$

Also, $B = 8\pi \times {10}^{- 4} = {\mu}_{0}H$

$∴ H = \dfrac{8\pi \times {10}^{- 4}}{{\mu}_{0}}$

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MH}}$

$I = \dfrac{MHT^{2}}{4{\pi}^{2}} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 8\pi \times {10}^{- 4} \times {15}^{2}}{4{\pi}^{2}{\mu}_{0}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 8\pi \times {10}^{- 4} \times 225}{4{\pi}^{2}{\left(4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\right)}^{2}}$

$I = \dfrac{2250 \times {10}^{- 9}}{\pi ( 16{\pi}^{2} ) \times {10}^{- 14}} = 4.54 \times {10}^{5}kgm^{2}$

questions.q: A hoop and a solid cylinder of same mass and radius are made of a permanent magnetic material with their respective axes. But the magnetic moment of hoop is twice of solid cylinder. They are placed in a uniform magnetic field in such a manner that their magnetic moments make a small angle with the field. If the oscillation periods of hoop and cylinder are ${T}_{h}$ and ${T}_{c}$ respectively, then:
questions.solution:
Time period of any magnetic body place in an external magnetic field is:-

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}}$

${T}_{hoop} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{mR^{2}}{MB}}$...... $( 1 ){I}_{hoop} = mR^{2}$

${T}_{c} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{mR^{2}}{2}}{\dfrac{M}{2}\left(B\right)}}$...... $( 2 ){I}_{Solidcylinder} = \dfrac{mR^{2}}{2}$

From $( 1 )$ and $( 2 )$

${T}_{h} = {T}_{c}$
